subject: error when stacking prediction projection matrix with covariates

messages.author: bb0d51bd5af5ac0d
messages.subject: error when stacking prediction projection matrix with covariates
parts:
I'm trying a variation of the example : Swiss rainfall data in section 6.10 of the book spatial and spatio-temporal data modeling with R-INLA,
where I wanted to include the covariate: elevation to do the prediction, due to the high number of prediction locations, I'm following the trick to project the latent field onto prediction grid locations.
As in this code:
A.est <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=Swiss.mesh, loc=est.coord)
A.val <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=Swiss.mesh) #, loc=val.coord
stack.val <- inla.stack(data = list(rain=NA),
                        A = list(A.val,1),
                        effects = list(c(s.index, list(Intercept=1)), list(Elevation=val.elevation)),
                        tag="val")

Because the A.val projection matrix has a smaller size, I got the error "Row count mismatch for A" in the stack.val. Is it possible to do the prediction with that covariate while using the trick here? I'm not sure how to assemble the inla.stack() if it could do. 
I'm also guessing, this trick might only available for the latent field?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] error when stacking prediction projection matrix with covariates
parts: You're right. when there's one covariate, the error message is :

Error in (function (data, A, effects, tag = "", compress = TRUE, remove.unused = TRUE)  : 
  Row count mismatch for A: 1394,13724

Sorry about that! (I actually have more than one covariate in my use case. To simplify the question I just paste the one covariate case. )
Seems like I have to make the covariate the same length with the mesh in order to proceed for big prediction data size. Then the question boils down to how do I choose the covariate indexes for prediction... which seems difficult.
A work around I could think is to get the posterior mean&sd of the coef for covariate from estimation model, then predict only the latent spatial field, then add the covariate part back? sounds very much complicated.
I guess I'm just looking for the most appropriate/direct way to get the prediction with covariate part.
